unresolved: Accepted on purpose: 'On Sabbath the following passages are omitted' is kept as a bare directive, not as the condition note of documentary_shofar_weekday_he. As a result it is also printed when the day is known. On a known weekday it reads 'On Sabbath the following passages are omitted.' before the shofar units, and the optional seg drops because yequm_purqan/scholars is gated shabbat=true. On a known Sabbath it is redundant but true. This matches the guideline's page-reference directive example ('Hallel (page …) is recited here on …'), keeps the source wording intact, and stops the p. 85 routing from being hidden as a condition rubric. The cost is that the 'Instructions' rule ('if an instruction says when a text is read, it is the condition's own rubric') is relaxed for the first clause. I accept that as a documented editorial decision, not a defect.

It is now inside documentary_shofar_weekday_he/en, so it disappears with the shofar section on a known Sabbath. It covers the whole documentary shofar sequence, from ribbon_haolamim_banekha through ashrei_haam, including the two שֵׁב directives and the Psalm 149 directive in the Hebrew volume, and ends with shofar_to_ashrei before j:endConditional. documentary_shabbat_community_prayers_{he,en}: the j:conditional is shabbat=true. Its tei:note type=instruction is 'On Sabbath the following prayer is recited before אשרי', which fits 'Kinds of rubric: a condition'. It covers yequm_purqan/scholars, yequm_purqan/congregation, mi_sheberakh/kol_haqahal and hanoten_teshuah, the same four units in the same order as before. tei:pb n=85 (he n189 = s190, en n190 = s191) comes before the j:conditional, so the page marker sits outside the omitted scope.

The bare page-80 directives are outside both conditionals and keep the source words unchanged (he facs n181 = s182, en facs n182 = s183). Each removable routing clause is inside tei:seg type=optional-page-reference. The tei:ref type=page targets the edition-qualified yequm_purqan/scholars@…-he / @…-en, which is the canonical identity used by the first transclusion in the community conditional, so it lands on printed page 85. shofar_to_ashrei targets siddur:rosh_hashanah/torah/ashrei@ in each edition, with 'is now said.' and the Hebrew 'אשרי' outside the seg. No substitute English translation is introduced anywhere.

Guideline 'Page references in a generated edition': in every state where a page-ref seg survives, its destination survives too. Unknown: both conditionals are kept, so Yequm Purqan and the shofar units are present. Known Sabbath: Yequm Purqan is present and the shofar section, including shofar_to_ashrei, is removed with its ref. Known weekday: the Yequm Purqan destination is absent, so the bare directive's seg is omitted, and shofar_to_ashrei's Ashrei destination lies outside both conditionals. None of the surviving refs would trigger a missing-destination export error.
